title: Service impact chronicle & customer update playbook (templates & examples)
body:
Purpose: a compact playbook for crafting customer-facing chronologies and status updates during service-impact events. Focus: brief, actionable, and non-technical summaries that customers can paste into support portals, status pages, or outbound emails. Use this as the single source for customer wording when the incident owner needs a quick draft.

How to use this doc:
- Pick the template that matches severity (minor degradation, partial outage, region-specific outage, full-service interruption).
- Fill placeholders: {{INCIDENT_ID}}, {{START_TIME}}, {{END_TIME}}, {{AFFECTED_FEATURES}}, {{CUSTOMER_SEGMENTS}}.
- Confirm: legal@redwood.ai and the SRE lead on-call have reviewed language for any claims about SLA credits.
- Publish: post to status page first, then send targeted emails for enterprise/dedicated/private customers.

Quick status update (status page / short Slack):
- Title: Service impact affecting {{AFFECTED_FEATURES}} — {{REGION}} — {{INCIDENT_ID}}
- Summary (1-2 sentences): We are currently investigating elevated error rates and increased latency for {{AFFECTED_FEATURES}} in {{REGION}}. Some requests may see timeouts or degraded responses.
- Impact: Approximately {{PERCENT}} of requests for customers in {{REGION}} experienced increased latency or errors. Hosted API keys were affected starting {{START_TIME}}.
- Mitigation steps in progress: routing adjustments, rolling restart of inference pool, temporary autoscaling to additional capacity.
- Next update: in 30 minutes or when the incident state changes.
- Link to details: status.redwood.ai/incidents/{{INCIDENT_ID}}

Customer-facing post-incident executive recap (concise, non-technical) — 3 paragraphs max:
1) What happened: On {{START_TIME}} we observed an unexpected service degradation that increased latencies and caused request errors for customers using {{AFFECTED_FEATURES}} in {{REGION}}.
2) What we did: Our SRE and serving teams implemented routing changes and added temporary capacity; we performed a controlled rollout of a compatibility patch and validated recovery metrics by {{END_TIME}}. Service returned to normal by {{END_TIME}}.
3) Next steps: We have opened a formal RCA and will share a follow-up with findings and any customer-specific remediation or credit guidance within 7 business days. If you were impacted and want a dedicated review, contact your TAM or support@redwood.ai.

Detailed timeline (customer digest): keep short; avoid raw logs. Use bullet time entries.
- {{START_TIME}} — First alerts: automated monitors flagged latency and elevated 5xx rates for requests routed to cluster-12.
- +6 minutes — Traffic re-routed away from cluster-12 to help mitigate impact (temporary measure).
- +18 minutes — Hotfix deployed to routing layer; partial reduction in error rate.
- +42 minutes — Autoscaling completed and additional nodes came online.
- {{END_TIME}} — Error rates returned to baseline; monitoring shows normal latency distribution for 15+ minutes.

Template: targeted email to Dedicated/Private customers (short):
Subject: Update on service disruption {{INCIDENT_ID}} — {{AFFECTED_FEATURES}}
Hi {{Customer Contact}},
We wanted to let you know about a recent disruption affecting {{AFFECTED_FEATURES}} in {{REGION}} between {{START_TIME}} and {{END_TIME}}. Our teams implemented mitigation measures and restored normal service by {{END_TIME}}. We will follow up with a concise RCA and any remediation steps or credits if applicable. If you’d like a post-incident technical briefing, reply to this message and we will schedule it.
Thanks for your patience,
Maya Thompson
Customer Success (Redwood Inference)

Template: status page update (short form to paste into CMS):
- header: [Resolved] Elevated latency and errors for {{AFFECTED_FEATURES}} — {{REGION}}
- body: We restored normal service at {{END_TIME}}. Root cause: a routing configuration regression combined with an unexpected cache invalidation pattern which caused a subset of inference workers to fallback to a slower execution path. Full customer-facing RCA will publish within 7 business days.

Template: longer public postmortem summary (customer friendly):
- Impact summary: Between {{START_TIME}} and {{END_TIME}}, customers in {{REGION}} experienced increased latency and errors impacting {{AFFECTED_FEATURES}}. Estimated percent of affected requests: {{PERCENT}}.
- Root cause (plain language): An internal routing configuration change caused a small group of inference workers to be assigned incompatible kernel configurations leading to degraded performance under typical workload patterns.
- Resolution (plain language): We reverted the configuration, removed the incompatible kernel selection, and added an automated check to detect similar regressions before rollout.
- Preventative actions and timeline for completion: automated pre-deploy validation (in progress — ETA 30 days), additional dashboard alerts for kernel mismatch (complete), targeted runbook updates (complete).

Customer communication checklist (internal):
- [ ] Draft status page message (this doc)
- [ ] Notify enterprise TAMs with targeted email and offer for briefing
- [ ] Check legal for statements about SLA credits
- [ ] Coordinate billing/finance if pro-rated credits are required
- [ ] If Private deployment impacted, inform platform-eng + in-region ops lead
- [ ] Schedule postmortem customer briefing (if > 1% of total requests impacted for a customer)

Escalation notes and who to loop in: keep terse.
- SRE on-call: @sre-oncall (primary)
- Serving runtime lead: Diego Alvarez
- Dedicated accounts lead (customer success): Sofia Patel
- Legal review: legal@redwood.ai (only if SLA language or contract-specific wording used)

Editable examples (for quick copy/paste):
- One-line: We experienced elevated latency and errors for {{AFFECTED_FEATURES}} in {{REGION}}; mitigation measures have been applied and service is restored.
- Two-line: We identified and corrected a routing configuration issue that impacted a subset of inference workers. Normal service resumed at {{END_TIME}}; a customer-friendly RCA is forthcoming.

Notes to author (internal editing):
- Avoid technical jargon (kernel, kv cache) in customer-facing text unless the customer explicitly requests a technical briefing.
- For Dedicated/Private customers include a summary of any data-plane implications and whether keys or data were unaffected.
- If credits are provided, include clear instructions and timelines for how customers receive them (billing contact, timeframe).

Open questions to resolve before final customer RCA:
- Was any persisted data or user content affected? (yes/no — confirm with infra)
- Do any enterprise contracts require advance notice or additional remediation? (check contract binder)
- Are there customers with custom routing who should receive an individualized note? (list from accounts team)

Follow-ups and retention:
- Publish customer-facing RCA to status.redwood.ai and link from customer emails.
- Archive internal timeline in CON-INC-{{INCIDENT_ID}} and attach to the ticket.
- Schedule a 1:1 with any impacted enterprise customer within 3 business days.

Ad-hoc templates (for specific scenarios):
- Partial feature regression: focus on feature-level mitigation (e.g., "Embeddings generation latency for long inputs") and include suggested temporary workarounds.
- Staggered region recovery: call out regions in order of recovery; customers may need to know which regions to avoid traffic to until fully recovered.

Draft footer to standardize contact info:
If you have questions about this event or want a private briefing, contact support@redwood.ai or your TAM. For legal or SLA questions, reference your contract and contact billing@redwood.ai.

Revision notes: created 2026-11-03 by Maya T. — internal review with SRE and serving runtime leads on 2026-11-04. This version intended to reduce back-and-forth for quick incidents and to standardize wording for enterprise communications.
